final_message:
I've drafted the September 2026 trend report for Bluebird Bakery for the reviewer. The analysis script ran without errors, and I wrote the commentary (8 bullets) into section 1; every figure in it comes from the script's output.

**Files** (in `evals/runs/v5-run-20261013/g_bb_no_ttm/skill_output/`):
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.md`: the draft report, with the DRAFT banner kept
- `bluebird-bakery-co-2026-09-trends.json`: the script's full output, which every figure in the report comes from

**Data quality: one mismatch, plus two places where the sheet's structure was reconstructed**
- The "Professional Services" subtotal for March 2026 says 2,225, but the accounts under it add up to 2,200 (a 25 difference). The analysis uses 2,200; the reviewer needs to decide which is right.
- The "Delivery" total has no section heading, so the script grouped the two accounts above it (Delivery Van Fuel and Courier: Same Day) under it because they add up to it every month.
- "Charitable Donations" has no figures and no total line, so it was counted as zero.
- September isn't flagged as a partial month.
- There are no trailing-twelve-month or year-over-year comparisons: the export covers only 9 months (Jan–Sep 2026). The report says this.

**Main points**
- **Revenue was 81,300 in September**, up 17.7% on August (69,050) and 17.3% above the average of the previous six months (69,292). Most of the increase is a new stream, Wholesale Accounts, at 12,000; it's zero in every earlier month. Whether it will recur is left for the reviewer.
- **Gross margin was 65.3%**, up 5.7 points on August and the highest month in the export.
- **Payroll & Benefits rose 28.4% to 22,600.** The whole 5,000 increase is in Wages & Salaries (16,000 to 21,000), after the category stayed at 17,600 from April to August. The reviewer should confirm whether it's a one-off or the new normal.
- **Cash in the bank fell to 37,600**: down 1,800 on August and 10,800 on six months earlier, even though net income was positive every month (21,553 in September). The commentary asks the reviewer to explain the outflow rather than guessing at a cause.

**Accounts in "Other":** Instagram Ads, Mystery Shopper Program and Supplier Rebates matched no category. Mystery Shopper Program appears in the table as 400 "from 0", but it was also 400 in March and June. The commentary describes it as a quarterly cost, not a new expense.
